Communities across Florida and Alabama
are in cleanup mode in the wake of Hurricane Isaias.
At least four people were killed
and hundreds of thousands of customers
left with no electricity.
NPR's Debbie Elliott reports.
Milton, Florida is a quaint and leafy town
northeast of Pensacola.
Now it's a big mess,
with trees uprooted and others snapped in two.
Fire Chief John E. Rebel says they're on houses,
in yards, and over roads.
What we're seeing is a result of wind,
and it was shocking how strong the winds were in this area.
Shocking because Milton is nearly 50 miles northwest
of where the hurricane made landfall.
Now the hum of generators is in the air,
and chainsaw crews are clearing trees from the roads.
President Karen Milstead says they'll get through.
Clean up and go on.
That could take a while.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Milton, Florida.
The U.S. Central Command says a fighter jet
used a precision weapon to hit a commercial cargo vessel
in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday.
The strike was part of the U.S. blockade
on Iranian shipping there.
Officials say the ship had left an Iranian port
and did not respond to repeated warnings.
The strike disabled the ship,
but did not harm any crew members.
President Trump was campaigning
in Clarksville, Tennessee Saturday night.
It's a state he won with 64% of the vote,
but voter displeasure with Trump
has made Tennessee a possible target for Democrats.
Trump suggested that Iran may attempt some sort of attack
before the midterm elections in November.
They'll probably do a little bit extra
before the election thinking it's gonna hurt us,
but we could end it really quick.
They don't know how nice I've been to them.
GOP candidates in Tennessee hope Trump's presence
will bring out Republican voters.
President Trump is facing pushback
for the administration's move
to sanction the International Criminal Court.
As Dan Karpenschuck reports,
Canada has joined several European countries
in supporting the international organization.
Canada signed a joint statement with Denmark,
Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, and Britain,
saying they disagree strongly with the sanctions
and reaffirmed their continued support
for the integrity of the international court.
They warned the sanctions would have a significant impact
on the work of the court in trying to bring those accused
of the most serious international crimes to justice.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called the court fake,
adding that Washington will cripple its ability
to operate against the US.
The White House wants to dismantle the tribunal
because of its investigations into the US and its allies,
namely Israel.
The sanctions were announced
after the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded
to South African jurist Navi Pillay on Friday.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Karpenschuck in Toronto.
And this is NPR News.
At least 12 people were killed Saturday,
including one American.
In an attack on the Saudi airport in Riyadh,
more than 300 other people were wounded
with a number of them listed in critical condition.
The attack is the latest in a series of strikes this week.
It was the deadliest attack in any Gulf Arab country
since the start of the Iran war.
A Saudi-led coalition is blaming Houthi rebels for the attack.
A new report in The Lancet says obesity is projected
to become one of the largest threats to human health
by the end of this century.
As NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports,
that's just one of 17 threats to global health,
the report identified.
Rather than focusing on a single threat,
the report brought together global data
on how over a dozen risk factors influence health.
Those factors are varied, including air pollution,
high blood pressure, and declining foreign aid.
The team estimated the number of years in good health
that could be lost because of each factor
over the next 75 years.
Over 23 billion years could be lost to obesity,
making it the biggest single threat.
Income inequality and low educational attainment
were the next biggest threats to health,
though both have substantial uncertainty.
To combat all these threats,
the report recommends bolstering health system readiness,
investing in new technologies,
and beefing up health surveillance.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
- Star soccer player Ronaldo has been suspended
by the Portuguese Soccer Federation
for walking out on the team.
The Federation has also begun disciplinary proceedings.
The 41-year-old Ronaldo left the Portugal camp
during a dispute with the team's new coach over playing time.
Ronaldo says he expects to be suspended
under Federation rules.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.
- This message comes from Charles Schwab
